interfaces.name: Norm
interfaces.type_shape: Lp random-variable norm; the un-subscripted norm in Conditions2.3–2.4 is L2, and its square is the second moment.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Lp random-variable norm; the un-subscripted norm in Conditions2.3–2.4 is L2, and its square is the second moment.

members.statement_original: For a random variable $Y$, write $Y\in L^p$, $p>0$, if $\|Y\|_p:=\mathbb E(|Y|^p)^{1/p}<\infty$. For $L^2$ norm write $\|\cdot\|=\|\cdot\|_2$.

interfaces.name: Causal representation
interfaces.type_shape: Time-dependent measurable causal maps of a two-sided iid innovation sequence. Maps may vary with t; no stationarity or smooth temporal variation is imposed. Mean zero is the separate Section2.2 convention archived in ambient context.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Time-dependent measurable causal maps of a two-sided iid innovation sequence. Maps may vary with t; no stationarity or smooth temporal variation is imposed. Mean zero is the separate Section2.2 convention archived in ambient context.

members.statement_original:
To characterize the non-stationary process $(X_t)$, we view $X_t$ as outputs from a physical system with the following causal representation:
\[
X_t=g_t(\mathcal F_t),\quad\text{with }\mathcal F_t=(\ldots,\varepsilon_{t-1},\varepsilon_t),
\]
(1.2)
where $(\varepsilon_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ are i. i. d. inputs of this system and $g_t:\mathbb R^\infty\to\mathbb R$ are measurable functions.

interfaces.name: Partial sums
interfaces.type_shape: Uncentered sum notation; Xi are mean zero in the approximation results. In T4.1 the inherited approximation is applied to noise Zi, so S_i there is the noise sum, not the noncentered observations.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Uncentered sum notation; Xi are mean zero in the approximation results. In T4.1 the inherited approximation is applied to noise Zi, so S_i there is the noise sum, not the noncentered observations.

interfaces.name: Common, possibly enriched probability space
interfaces.type_shape: Existence of a coupling with an equal-joint-law copy on an enriched space. Not an independent Gaussian on the original probability space or an asserted almost-sure approximation.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Existence of a coupling with an equal-joint-law copy on an enriched space. Not an independent Gaussian on the original probability space or an asserted almost-sure approximation.

members.statement_original: Note that in principle such Gaussian approximations for random variables $(X_i)_{i=1}^n$ require a common, possibly enriched probability space $(\Phi_c,\mathcal A_c,\mathbb P_c)$ on which the approximating Gaussian processes and random variables $(X_i^c)_{1\le i\le n}=_{\mathcal D}(X_i)_{1\le i\le n}$ can be defined. In order for better readability, we omit this technicality and simply state our results in terms of the original random variables $X_i$’s.

interfaces.name: Uniform functional dependence
interfaces.type_shape: Replace one innovation by an independent copy and take the Lp difference uniformly over time. Not a mixing coefficient or replacement of the whole past.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Replace one innovation by an independent copy and take the Lp difference uniformly over time. Not a mixing coefficient or replacement of the whole past.

members.statement_original:
With this system, given $k\ge0$, a time lag, we measure the dependence from how much the outputs $X_i$ of this system will change if we replace the input information at time $i-k$ with an i.i.d. copy $\varepsilon'_{i-k}$. For $p\ge1$, define the uniform functional dependence
\[
\delta_p(k):=\sup_i(\mathbb E|X_i-X_{i,\{i-k\}}|^p)^{1/p},\quad\text{where }X_{i,\{i-k\}}=g_i(\ldots,\varepsilon_{i-k-1},\varepsilon'_{i-k},\varepsilon_{i-k+1},\ldots,\varepsilon_i)
\]
(2.3)
is a coupled version of $X_i$.

interfaces.name: Dependence condition
interfaces.type_shape: Tail sum of uniform functional-dependence coefficients, not a single-lag coefficient.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Tail sum of uniform functional-dependence coefficients, not a single-lag coefficient.

members.statement_original:
we will express our dependence condition in terms of
\[
\Theta_{i,p}=\sum_{k=i}^\infty\delta_p(k),\quad i\ge0.
\]
(2.4)

interfaces.name: Uniform dependency-adjusted norm
interfaces.type_shape: Uniform polynomial decay of dependence tails. Theorem-specific A cutoffs are separate. The p>4 branch of T3.1 also uses this norm at moment order4.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Uniform polynomial decay of dependence tails. Theorem-specific A cutoffs are separate. The p>4 branch of T3.1 also uses this norm at moment order4.

members.statement_original:
Consider (1.2). Suppose that $\Theta_{0,p}<\infty$ for some $p>2$. Assume there exists $A>1$ and constant $C>0$, such that the uniform dependency-adjusted norm
\[
\mu_{p,A}:=\sup_{i\ge0}(i+1)^A\Theta_{i,p}\le C<\infty.
\]
(2.5)

interfaces.name: Truncated uniform integrability condition
interfaces.type_shape: Printed supremum over i with truncation an for every fixed a>0. Keep the p parameter shared with Condition2.1 without adding decay as a dependency of integrability itself. The source’s claim that this is weaker than classical UI is recorded separately.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Printed supremum over i with truncation an for every fixed a>0. Keep the p parameter shared with Condition2.1 without adding decay as a dependency of integrability itself. The source’s claim that this is weaker than classical UI is recorded separately.

members.statement_original:
For the same $p$ as in Condition 2.1, the series $(|X_i|^p)$ satisfies the truncated uniform integrability condition:
For any fixed $a>0$, $\sup_i\mathbb E(|X_i|^p\mathbb I_{\{|X_i|^p\ge an\}})\to0$ as $n\to\infty$.

interfaces.name: Non-singularity condition
interfaces.type_shape: Uniform divergence of every increasing-block second moment, with m_n+1 terms as printed. No linear-in-length lower bound is asserted.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Uniform divergence of every increasing-block second moment, with m_n+1 terms as printed. No linear-in-length lower bound is asserted.

members.statement_original: For all sequences $(m_n)\in\mathbb N$ with $m_n\to\infty$ and $m_n<n$, the process $(X_i)$ satisfies that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\min_{1\le i\le n-m_n}\|X_i+\ldots+X_{i+m_n}\|^2=\infty$.

naming_context.text: This non-singularity condition is a very natural one.

interfaces.name: Truncated partial sum process
interfaces.type_shape: Winsorization at n^(1/p) followed by explicit centering in the partial sums. Covariance matching in T2.2 uses winsorized variables; its approximation still targets the original partial sums.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Winsorization at n^(1/p) followed by explicit centering in the partial sums. Covariance matching in T2.2 uses winsorized variables; its approximation still targets the original partial sums.

naming_context.text: we begin by presenting a Gaussian approximation for the truncated partial sum process

interfaces.name: Non-singularity condition
interfaces.type_shape: Uniform linear lower bound on block second moments, stronger than Condition2.3. The printed range leaves l≤n implicit; empty minima are not assigned invented values.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Uniform linear lower bound on block second moments, stronger than Condition2.3. The printed range leaves l≤n implicit; empty minima are not assigned invented values.

members.statement_original: The series $(X_i)$ satisfies the following condition: There exists a constant $c>0$ and $l_0\in\mathbb N$, such that for all $l\ge l_0$, $\min_{1\le j\le n-l+1}\|X_j+\ldots+X_{j+l-1}\|^2/l\ge c$.

interfaces.name: Quadratic large deviation bounds
interfaces.type_shape: Banded upper-triangular quadratic form, partitioned by its terminal index and centered blockwise. D_n is a positive integer bandwidth for these sums, though the statement only explicitly prints D_n≤n. R_k is distinct from the earlier residual block sum R_j.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Banded upper-triangular quadratic form, partitioned by its terminal index and centered blockwise. D_n is a positive integer bandwidth for these sums, though the statement only explicitly prints D_n≤n. R_k is distinct from the earlier residual block sum R_j.

members.statement_original:
Let $Q_n=\sum_{1\le s\le t\le n}a_{s,t}X_sX_t$, with $a_{s,t}=0$ if $|s-t|>D_n$ for some $D_n\le n$, and $\sup|a_{s,t}|\le1$. Denote
\[
R_k=\sum_{j=1}^k(V_j-\mathbb E(V_j)),\quad\text{where }V_k=\sum_{t=(k-1)D_n+1}^{(kD_n)\wedge n}\sum_{1\le s\le t}a_{s,t}X_sX_t,\quad\text{for }1\le k\le\lceil n/D_n\rceil.
\]
(3.3)

naming_context.text: Quadratic large deviation bounds have a long history that started with the seminal work by Hanson and Wright [47] and Wright [100].

interfaces.name: Signal-plus-noise model
interfaces.type_shape: Observed signal-plus-noise data. The Gaussian approximation assumptions apply to centered noise Zi, not observations Xi with a varying mean.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Observed signal-plus-noise data. The Gaussian approximation assumptions apply to centered noise Zi, not observations Xi with a varying mean.

interfaces.name: Grid
interfaces.type_shape: Deterministic quantile design from a smooth density. The printed strict endpoint grid conflicts with t_n=F^-1(1)=1; retain both passages and flag the endpoint convention.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Deterministic quantile design from a smooth density. The printed strict endpoint grid conflicts with t_n=F^-1(1)=1; retain both passages and flag the endpoint convention.

members.statement_original:
Let $0=t_0<t_1<t_2<\ldots<t_{n-1}<t_n<t_{n+1}=1$ be an $n$-length grid on $[0,1]$.
Here we let $t_i=F^{-1}(i/n)$, where $F(t)=\int_0^tf(u)\,du$ for some density $f\in C^3[0,1]$.

interfaces.name: Smooth symmetric kernel
interfaces.type_shape: Smooth symmetric compactly supported kernel with integrated modulus condition. Normalization and denominator nondegeneracy are customary but not separately stated in this passage.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Smooth symmetric compactly supported kernel with integrated modulus condition. Normalization and denominator nondegeneracy are customary but not separately stated in this passage.

members.statement_original:
Assume that $K$ is a smooth symmetric kernel with bounded support $[-\omega,\omega]$, satisfying:
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\Psi_K(u;\delta)\,du=O(\delta)\text{ as }\delta\to0,\quad\text{where }\Psi_K(u;\delta)=\sup\{|K(y)-K(u)|:|y-u|\le\delta\}.
\]
(4.9)

interfaces.name: Local linear estimate
interfaces.type_shape: Local linear smoother using deterministic design and kernel moments. S_j(t) denotes weighted design moments, distinct from stochastic partial sums S_i. Same weights are applied to the Gaussian noise in T4.1.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Local linear smoother using deterministic design and kernel moments. S_j(t) denotes weighted design moments, distinct from stochastic partial sums S_i. Same weights are applied to the Gaussian noise in T4.1.

members.statement_original:
Define
\[
S_j(t)=\sum_{i=1}^n(t-t_i)^jK((t-t_i)/h_n).
\]
(4.7)
Theorem 4.1 below provides a Gaussian approximation for the local linear estimate
\[
\widehat\mu_{h_n}(t):=\sum_{i=1}^nw_{h_n}(t,i)X_i,\quad\text{where }w_{h_n}(t,i)=K\left(\frac{t-t_i}{h_n}\right)\frac{S_2(t)-(t-t_i)S_1(t)}{S_2(t)S_0(t)-S_1^2(t)}.
\]
(4.8)
